analysis.title: GS - Macro Reads (Arvin Joseph, 1 Nov 2026)
key_insights: GS sees the broad Dollar range-bound in October despite a meaningful Euro decline. Risks are tilted to further Euro weakening, driven by a EUR-specific risk premium. GS prefers Yen (G10) and Shekel (EM) as hedges over the Dollar, because equity pressure is concentrated in tech.
GS expects the CNY fix to keep strengthening and forecasts CNY will erase all of its post-pandemic losses over the coming year, citing ongoing trade surpluses and firm Asian currency management.

GS says a GPIF asset allocation change that would support JPY is unlikely before Spring 2027. GPIF results as of end-September 2026 are due November 6 (local time). GS favors short EUR/JPY over the shorter term and sees USD/JPY lower over the longer term.

RBNZ held rates in October against near-unanimous economist expectations and market pricing for a hike, and NZD underperformed. GS economists expect further hikes in December and March. GS closes its AUD/NZD puts and keeps EUR/AUD shorts, because terms of trade (energy) are the dominant driver of AUD/NZD.

New Zealand holds a general election on Nov 7. A majority for either National or Labour looks unlikely per prediction markets. GS sees a reversion to an RBNZ dual mandate (Labour proposal) and protracted coalition talks as negatives for NZD.

In rates, GS closes its receive 10s on the 5s10s30s SOFR fly and adds a long 5s on the 2s5s30s UST fly (entry -44bp, target -60bp, stop -35bp). GS sees runway for the rally to extend if risk asset volatility persists.

GS expects an ECB hike in December and the BoE to hike next week. A December BoJ hike looks likely, and GS GIR moved its BoJ hike forecast from January to December. An RBA hike is likely next week. RBNZ's hold favors 2s10s NZD steepening.

GS Prime: hedge funds net bought US equities for the first time in 4 weeks, driven by short covers. Info Tech is still heavily net sold month to date, and Mag 7 were net sold in 4 of the last 5 sessions.

The US equity sell-off on Friday looked systematic and top-down driven, with ETFs at about 31% of tape, the highest full-session level since June. GS watches the S&P 100dma (7614) and the CTA medium-term threshold (7554).
The Russell 2000 outperformed the NDX and SPX in a tech-led sell-off. GS systematic momentum thresholds would flip negative if Friday's price action persists, which would halt projected CTA buying.

Front-end NDX and SPX vols fell sharply during the week (NDX 1m fixed strike vol down almost 4 vols), then rose almost 2 vols on Friday. The straddle through Wednesday's close implied 1.51% against a 1.82% decline in the S&P on Friday alone.

Ahead of the midterms, GS outlines affordability-themed baskets: long ACA-exposed beneficiaries, short drug-makers, long renewables/grid/power, buy protection on Hyperscalers and Datacenter Equipment, and long government-spending exposed vs short defense beneficiaries.

Korea: KOSPI rebounded 3% and 12m-forward EPS was revised up 3.3%. Buybacks and treasury-share cancellations accelerated in 2026. Pension funds net bought US$668mn on Oct 30, their second-largest single-day net purchase. Historically the largest such day was followed by a median 12-month KOSPI return of 17% and an average of 33%.

GS Portfolio Strategy: with 60% of S&P 500 companies reported, Q3 2026 EPS growth is on track for 33% y/y. Excluding non-recurring items, GS expects growth of nearly 30% in 2026 slowing to 18% in 2027. GS says AI capex growth is peaking. Hyperscaler capex is about $800B this year (+96% y/y) and estimated at $1.2T in 2027 (+44%).

GS FICC trade ideas: buy a 3m USDCNH 6.525 digital put, buy a 1Q27 TTF 125/150 call spread, buy 6y South African government bonds (SAGB 2032s) on asset swap ahead of an ALBI duration change, and short EUR financials AT1 bonds as a hedge for long European bank equity.

European gas trades firmly as LNG flows through the Strait hold at roughly 30% of pre-conflict levels, and temperatures forecast 2-3°C below seasonal norms into early November. GIR's tail scenario for TTF is EUR 150.

US Q3 ECI rose 0.8% (not annualized), in line with expectations. GS's preferred private wages and salaries ex-incentive-paid measure rose 0.7%. The GS Q3 wage tracker stands at 3.0% y/y, below the pace consistent with 2% inflation.
Taiwan Q3 real GDP grew 3.2% qoq sa. GS raised its 2026 and 2027 Taiwan GDP forecasts to 13.0% and 6.3% from 11.7% and 3.3%, versus Bloomberg consensus of 11.4% and 5.1%.

The PBOC moved its policy rate to the overnight reverse repo rate (1.25%, 15bp below the 7-day rate of 1.40%), effective 2 November, after credit flare-ups. GS expects Chinese government bond yields and swap rates to grind lower.

sector_views.rationale: Equity pressure is concentrated in tech. Hedge funds remain heavy net sellers of Info Tech month to date and Mag 7 were net sold in 4 of the last 5 sessions.

earnings_insights: S&P 500 Q3 2026 EPS growth is on track for 33% y/y with 60% of companies reported (GS estimate, excluding nothing stated for this figure). GS expects 2026 EPS growth of nearly 30% excluding non-recurring items, slowing to 18% in 2027.
Korea's two largest memory makers (SK Hynix, SEC) reported strong earnings. KOSPI 12m-forward EPS was revised up 3.3%.

trade_ideas.description: Short EUR/JPY over the shorter term
trade_ideas.rationale: GS sees several EUR-negative risks in the months ahead and possible JPY support from GPIF allocation shifts.

trade_ideas.description: Short EUR/AUD, thesis of divergent fiscal and energy terms of trade, with a modest carry buffer (AUD/NZD puts closed)
trade_ideas.rationale: Energy terms of trade favor AUD over NZD and EUR.

trade_ideas.description: Long 5s on the 2s5s30s UST fly (entry -44bp, target -60bp, stop -35bp); close receive 10s on the 5s10s30s SOFR fly
trade_ideas.rationale: Runway for the rally to extend if risk asset volatility persists.
RBNZ held despite a largely priced hike, in contrast to the flatter AUD curve ahead of a likely RBA hike.

trade_ideas.description: Buy 3m USDCNH 6.525 digital put for 10.00% USD (~10x max leverage)
trade_ideas.rationale: CNH keeps strengthening on PBoC fixing bias, undervaluation and exporter conversion, and USDCNH vol is cheap.

trade_ideas.description: Buy 1Q27 TTF 125/150 call spread for 3.85/MWh (~6.5x max leverage)
trade_ideas.rationale: LNG flows are about 30% of pre-conflict levels, colder weather and thin storage. GIR tail scenario is EUR 150.

trade_ideas.description: Buy SAGB 2032s on asset swap at -47bps (target -32bps), or outright targeting >50-70bps over a year
trade_ideas.rationale: ALBI duration extension on Nov 5 and removal of R188 and TN27 should create about 500-700k dv01 of demand for 6y SAGBs.
trade_ideas.risk: If the 40bps of hikes priced in SA 1y do not materialise the outright trade is favored, so the risk is hikes being delivered.

trade_ideas.description: Short EUR Financials AT1 (CoCo) bonds via TRS on iBoxx EUR AT1 Index (C2D1) or GS EUR AT1 Bond Basket (GSLCHAT1), rates hedged, as a hedge for long European bank equity
trade_ideas.rationale: AT1 spreads screen tight, have outperformed SX7E in the risk-off, and are cheaper than bank equity puts as a tail hedge.

trade_ideas.description: Long ACA-exposed beneficiaries (GSHLCACA); short drug-makers (GSHLCBPH); long renewables (GSXURNEW), grid infrastructure (GSXUGRID), Power Up America (GSENEPOW); buy protection on Hyperscalers (GSXUHYPR) and Datacenter Equipment (GSTMTDAT); long government-spending exposed ex-defense and drug-makers (GSXUGOVT) vs short defense beneficiaries (GSXUDFNS)
trade_ideas.rationale: Affordability concerns will remain top-of-mind into the midterms.

US midterm elections in November and related affordability themes.
